messages:
morgan: Odd bundler/edge failure when trying to run the JS SDK from our starter template. Build passes but worker crashes with `TypeError: Super expression must either be null or a function`.

morgan: App is ESM (`type: "module"`) and import is `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'`. Repro only when building with rollup (vite uses rollup under the hood for lib mode).

anya: do you have the package exports block handy? conditional exports often cause resolver differences.

morgan: exports look like: `{".":{"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs","types":"./dist/types/index.d.ts"}}`.

jamie: that pattern can cause rollup-plugin-node-resolve to pick the CJS entry and then commonjs transform wraps it weirdly. Edge runtimes are strict about subclassing across wrappers which explains the super expression error.

riley: quick repro steps I used: 1) clone minimal-edge-starter, 2) npm i, 3) npm run build, 4) run miniflare. Fails on startup.

morgan: tried `commonjs({ transformMixedEsModules: true })` and it removed the super error but then I hit `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default')`.

oliver: interim workaround that worked for me: add a vite/rollup alias to the explicit ESM file: `alias: { '@redwood/inference': 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js' }`. Not ideal but unblocks onboarding.

anya: we should add a short note in the starter README with that alias + a one-liner explaining it's a bundler resolution quirk. Saves new hires an hour.

jamie: SDK action items: (1) ensure exports are resolvable by vite/rollup/esbuild resolvers, (2) consider adding a top-level `module` or explicit `.mjs` ESM files so bundlers prefer the ESM path, (3) expose `types` at top-level or via `exports.types` for reliable `import type` resolution, (4) add a sample-app CI job that builds with vite/rollup and runs miniflare smoke.

sdk-bot: Created RED-PLAT/SDK#1722 by morgan: "Bundler resolution picks CJS wrapper; breaks subclassing in edge runtime"

riley: also mention in the issue to test different import forms (`import default`, `import * as`, and `require`) because bundlers can treat them differently.

morgan: I'll open a small README PR with the alias workaround and link the SDK issue. When SDK fixes, we'll remove the workaround and add migration notes for pinned versions.

jamie: thanks. adding a short CI task to sample-apps to build with latest vite + rollup and run miniflare should catch regressions early.

morgan: will follow up with PR + issue updates. :thumbsup:
